BOBBY WORKBOOK TASK 5 (Sept 30). Bobby executes under Kevin. Goal: identify what is insured today, whether KMD's lab operations are covered, and what must be added or replaced. Review the building owner's coverage separately from KMD's.

Steps: (1) Collect all policies: declarations, forms, endorsements, exclusions, schedules, renewals, plus the lease insurance requirements; a certificate alone is not the policy. (2) Inventory each policy: insurer, number, named insured, additional insureds, address, dates, limits, deductibles, exclusions, premium, covered operations; mark unknowns 'not confirmed'. (3) Put redacted documents into the approved AI workspace; ask for a gap table with exact policy references (employee injuries, visitor injuries, property damage, testing errors, chemical incidents). (4) Broker to confirm KMD's entity and lab operations are covered: general liability, business personal property and instruments, equipment breakdown, business interruption, professional liability for testing, chemical/pollution exclusions; discuss cyber, umbrella, customer samples in custody. (5) Compare with the lease; confirm additional-insured endorsements; do not assume the owner's building policy covers KMD. (6) Get written answers and quotes for gaps; bind through the authorized process; keep existing coverage until replacement is effective.
Done when: inventory and gap review saved, broker has confirmed material questions in writing, changes active or tracked with an exact next step.

AI PROMPT (copy into Claude):
"Review these redacted insurance policies and lease requirements for KMD Analytical, a California analytical testing laboratory. Build a table with risk, relevant policy, named insured, location, limit, exclusion, exact page or endorsement, uncertainty, and broker question. Check employee injury, visitor injury, property and lab instruments, equipment failure, interrupted operations, testing errors, chemical incidents, and customer samples. Distinguish landlord coverage from tenant coverage. If documents are missing, say so. Do not promise that a claim is covered; draft precise questions for the licensed broker and recommend coverage types to discuss."
